findings.description: Direct inspection of all current views still shows a plain ivory jacket with a broad lavender diagonal chest stripe, sparse closures, oversized elbow diamonds, and faceted torso, sleeves, skirt, and rear surfaces; the distinctive finished fencing-practice styling is absent.

The v11 hem is visibly shorter at the standing front, but the skirt still reads as a broad low-detail flared shell; the sewn pleat structure is not legible as an articulated fencing skirt and the rear/side panels remain faceted.

Current crouch and seated renders show substantial shorts exposure as the overskirt lifts behind and beside the thighs. The current geometric overskirt ray-coverage fractions on left/right upper thigh are neutral 0.3593/0.3605, crouch 0.2802/0.2780, and sit 0.2452/0.2475; these values are prototype geometry evidence only and do not grant fit acceptance.

The prone render still compresses the skirt into a wide uneven fan, while crouch and seated views show rigid triangular folds and extensive shorts exposure. The shorter hem hypothesis has not resolved posed drape or coverage.
Arms-up and arm-cross views retain visible sleeve and underarm faceting; elbow diamonds remain oversized surface decals rather than restrained quilted patches.
Rear and side views remain featureless and faceted with an abrupt waist-to-skirt transition and no convincing rear adjustment or finished panel detail.

sourceEvidence.currentPrototypeMotif: Direct review of the v11 short-hem sewn-pleat renders confirms a shorter standing hem, but the overskirt remains broadly flared, posed coverage and drape remain poor, and the jacket, elbow details, rear finish, and faceted surfaces remain below acceptance.

nextAction: REJECT; revise the pattern and sewn panel construction so the short skirt has readable controlled pleats and stays covering the shorts in crouch, sit, and prone poses; refine jacket, rear and side details and reduce surface faceting, then produce a new revision for direct review.
